text: Increase uniform same-user negative sampling from K=4 to K=8 in the pairwise logistic ranker.
rationale: Experiment 4 improved primary over experiment 3 by 0.00043 while increasing K from 1 to 4, with both GAUC and nDCG@5 improving. A larger but still bounded negative set may expose additional within-user inversions.
exact_ablation: Change only the number of uniformly sampled same-user negatives per eligible positive from K=4 to K=8, without replacement when available; retain the additive five-field scorer, pairwise logistic loss, optimizer, regularization, epochs, and stopping rule.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase by 0.0001 to 0.0010 from broader within-user positive-negative coverage.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase by 0.0001 to 0.0008 if additional comparisons correct high-rank inversions.

text: Reduce uniform same-user negative sampling from K=4 to K=2 in the pairwise logistic ranker.
rationale: The gain from K=1 to K=4 was small, so K=4 may already include noisy or redundant comparisons. A smaller K is a clean test of whether more focused updates improve top-five ordering.
exact_ablation: Change only the number of uniformly sampled same-user negatives per eligible positive from K=4 to K=2, without replacement when available; retain all other model, loss, optimizer, regularization, and stopping settings.

expected_effect.GAUC: Change by -0.0003 to 0.0007; fewer comparisons may slightly reduce broad ordering coverage.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase by 0.0000 to 0.0010 if reduced redundant-negative pressure better preserves top-five ordering.

text: Use dynamic hardest same-user negative sampling instead of uniform negative sampling.
rationale: Experiment 4 has strong overall GAUC but modest nDCG@5, suggesting remaining mistakes may be concentrated among high-scoring negatives. Mining the currently highest-scored eligible negative directly targets those inversions without adding features.
exact_ablation: Replace only uniform K=4 same-user negative sampling with dynamic selection of the four highest-current-score negative training rows for each eligible positive, recomputed once per epoch; retain the five-field additive scorer, pairwise logistic loss, optimizer, regularization, and stopping rule.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase by 0.0002 to 0.0015 because updates focus on difficult within-user negatives.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase by 0.0004 to 0.0020 because hard-negative training preferentially targets errors near the top of a user's ranked list.

text: Add a low-cardinality tab-by-hour categorical interaction to the additive pairwise ranker.
rationale: Request context is the only positively screened feature family, with full coverage and positive temporal-screen lift. Unlike the failed high-cardinality user-by-tab feature, tab-by-hour is a compact context-only interaction and can model time-varying request surfaces.
exact_ablation: Append exactly one train-fitted categorical feature formed by the pair (tab, hour), with an unknown bucket; retain the five existing fields, additive scorer, K=4 uniform pair construction, pairwise logistic loss, optimizer, regularization, and stopping rule.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase by 0.0001 to 0.0012 if context-specific item ordering differs by hour.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase by 0.0002 to 0.0015 if the compact interaction improves ordering in top-five request contexts.

text: Increase L2 regularization of the additive pairwise model from 1e-6 to 1e-5.
rationale: The user-by-tab expansion degraded primary by 0.00209 versus experiment 4, consistent with sensitivity to sparse ID effects. Stronger shrinkage is a single conservative adjustment that may improve temporal generalization without adding features.
exact_ablation: Change only the L2 coefficient from 0.000001 to 0.00001; retain features, additive architecture, K=4 uniform pair sampling, pairwise logistic loss, learning rate, batch size, epoch budget, and stopping rule.

expected_effect.GAUC: Change by -0.0002 to 0.0008 as shrinkage may reduce overfit to sparse identifiers.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Change by -0.0001 to 0.0010 if regularization prevents unstable top-rank score shifts.

text: Decrease L2 regularization of the additive pairwise model from 1e-6 to 1e-7.
rationale: Experiment 4's best retained model is deliberately simple and may be mildly underfit on warm items, which account for 121,510 validation rows. A one-order reduction tests whether its ID coefficients benefit from less shrinkage.
exact_ablation: Change only the L2 coefficient from 0.000001 to 0.0000001; retain features, additive architecture, K=4 uniform pair sampling, pairwise logistic loss, learning rate, batch size, epoch budget, and stopping rule.

expected_effect.GAUC: Change by -0.0004 to 0.0008; less shrinkage can improve fitted within-user ordering but may overfit.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Change by -0.0005 to 0.0008; any benefit is expected mainly for abundant warm-item comparisons.

text: Lower the Adam learning rate from 0.01 to 0.005 for the retained pairwise ranker.
rationale: Official gains from the pairwise objective are small, so optimizer-step noise can plausibly dominate incremental changes. A lower learning rate is a directly interpretable optimization ablation with no feature or leakage implications.
exact_ablation: Change only the Adam learning rate from 0.01 to 0.005; retain the five-field additive scorer, K=4 uniform pair construction, pairwise logistic loss, L2 coefficient, batch size, epoch budget, and stopping rule.

expected_effect.GAUC: Change by -0.0002 to 0.0009 through potentially more stable convergence.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Change by -0.0001 to 0.0010 if stability improves ordering near rank five.

text: Increase the maximum epoch budget from 10 to 20 while retaining validation GAUC early stopping.
rationale: Experiment 4 uses validation-based early stopping, so increasing only the ceiling safely tests whether optimization was prematurely capped while preserving the existing checkpoint-selection mechanism.
exact_ablation: Change only max_epochs from 10 to 20; retain the five-field additive scorer, K=4 uniform sampling, pairwise logistic loss, optimizer, regularization, patience, and validation-GAUC checkpoint rule.

expected_effect.GAUC: Change by 0.0000 to 0.0010 if a later checkpoint improves within-user discrimination.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Change by -0.0001 to 0.0008 because stopping selects GAUC rather than nDCG@5 directly.

text: Select the early-stopping checkpoint by validation primary instead of validation GAUC.
rationale: The official selection objective is primary, whereas the current trainer stops on a GAUC proxy. Since experiment 4's nDCG@5 is lower than its GAUC, matching checkpoint selection to primary may recover a better GAUC/nDCG trade-off without changing training updates.
exact_ablation: Change only checkpoint selection and early stopping from validation within-user GAUC to validation primary, computed as the mean of official GAUC and nDCG@5; retain all data, features, model parameters, pair sampling, loss, optimizer, and patience.

expected_effect.GAUC: Change by -0.0005 to 0.0005 because primary selection may accept a slightly lower-GAUC checkpoint.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase by 0.0002 to 0.0015 because selection explicitly values top-five ranking.

text: Replace independent K=4 pair losses with one per-positive multi-negative softmax loss.
rationale: Experiment 4's K=4 pairs modestly improved both official metrics. A grouped loss over the same positive and sampled negatives may emphasize selecting the positive over the full local competitor set, which is closer to top-list competition.
exact_ablation: Replace only the sum of independent pairwise logistic losses for each positive and its K=4 sampled negatives with a grouped softmax loss that places the positive score against those same four negative scores; retain features, K=4 uniform sampling, optimizer, regularization, and stopping rule.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase by 0.0000 to 0.0012 through better local comparative ordering.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase by 0.0003 to 0.0018 because grouped competition may better prioritize positive items over several alternatives.

text: Train a rank-8 second-order factorization machine over the retained five fields using the current pairwise setup.
rationale: The rank-16 factorization machine under pointwise BCE was worse than the additive model, but the pairwise objective improved over pointwise BCE. A lower-rank interaction model under the retained ranking objective tests whether limited interactions can help without the larger capacity that previously regressed.
exact_ablation: Replace only the additive logit with a rank-8 second-order factorization-machine logit over exactly user_id, video_id, tab, hour, and weekday; retain K=4 uniform same-user pair construction, pairwise logistic loss, optimizer family, regularization, and stopping rule.

expected_effect.GAUC: Change by -0.0008 to 0.0012; limited interactions may correct remaining preference-context inversions but prior FM evidence is unfavorable.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Change by -0.0006 to 0.0015; any lift would arise from moving contextually relevant items into the first five positions.

text: Add a low-cardinality hour-by-weekday categorical interaction to the additive pairwise ranker.
rationale: Request context had stable positive train-only temporal-screen lift, while the weak validation behavior varies substantially by hour. Hour-by-weekday is a compact, impression-time context interaction that avoids the failed user-specific interaction family.
exact_ablation: Append exactly one train-fitted categorical feature formed by the pair (hour, weekday), with an unknown bucket; retain five existing fields, additive scorer, K=4 uniform pair sampling, pairwise logistic loss, optimizer, regularization, and stopping rule.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase by 0.0001 to 0.0010 if temporal request patterns alter within-user item ordering.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase by 0.0002 to 0.0013 if the temporal interaction improves the highest-ranked impressions in weaker hours.
